title: The projection says which path each video took (R1008 slice 3)
body:
Slice 3 of `docs/plans/oracle/capped-whole-transcript-path.md` — **OD-13**, **R28**, **R1008**. The last slice. Follows #186 and #187.

### What it does

`Projection` gains the routing figures and `project` gains a `submissions` parameter. The printed checkpoint now says how many videos went whole and how many as excerpts, the characters and projected tokens each path accounts for, how many whole transcripts exceed one bundle's cap, and each of those by id with the number of bundles it spans. The owner can see the uncapped path's largest submissions before anything is spent.

**The path figures come from the SUBMISSIONS; the span figures come from the BUNDLES.** A bundle cannot say why a video is on the excerpt path, and a part count cannot say what actually happened to the parts — so `bundles_spanned` counts the distinct bundles holding a whole-form block of that video, which is what the transcript SPANS rather than what the router intended.

**The cap is printed beside the spans**, for the same reason the chars-per-token factor is printed beside the totals: a span reported without the bound that produced it invites the reader to treat it as a property of the corpus rather than of the configuration.

`excerpt_characters` keeps its name and narrows to excerpt-form text; `whole_characters` is the whole-form text; the two sum to what the old field counted, so a reader comparing runs across this change is not silently comparing different quantities. `whole_tokens` and `excerpt_tokens` split the projected tokens the same way.

### Blind test authorship

`Blind-Tests: capped-whole-transcript-path-3`. **45 cases added** to `tests/test_estimate.py` by a separate agent in a worktree pinned to slice 2's tip.

Its core fixture is five submissions built by the **real** `choose_submission`, `split_whole` and `pack_bundles` at one char per token and a 40-token cap: two whole videos spanning 2 and 3 bundles, one whole video fitting in 1, one excerpt-path video, and one contributing no blocks at all. Eight blocks over five videos, so a block count is visibly wrong; the ids are non-alphabetical and the two spans differ in size, so neither sort order reproduces the expected span tuple by accident.

Proved under **12 deliberate mutations**, each failing exactly the tests that name it: counting blocks not videos, `bundles_spanned` from `part_count`, `bundles_spanned` counting blocks not bundles, single-bundle videos left in the span list, `excerpt_characters` counting both forms, `excerpt_characters` over every submission, `whole_characters` from the transcript rather than the blocks, double-counted tokens, the span list sorted by id, the cap omitted from the render, an empty corpus raising instead of reporting zeroes, and — the one that matters most — **`videos_over_bundle_cap` computed from the bundles**, which would make the cross-check vacuous. That last mutation is caught by exactly one test.

**All 1499 tests passed against this implementation on the first assembly.** Three slices, three clean first runs.

### The plan's own cross-check is not universally true, and the blind author found why

`videos_over_bundle_cap == len(bundles_spanned)` holds on a normal run. It does **not** hold in one edge case the plan itself creates: a cue is never split, an over-cap cue becomes a part on its own, and `pack_bundles` gives it a bundle to itself — so a whole-path video can exceed `bundle_token_cap` while occupying exactly **one** bundle. Over the cap, spanning nothing.

The blind author asserted the equality on a normal run and the *definition* separately on that edge case, because collapsing them would make the "computed from the bundles too" mutation undetectable. This implementation derives `videos_over_bundle_cap` from the submissions' own recorded transcript length, so both hold.

### Two files outside this slice's Files list

Both unavoidable, both flagged independently by the blind author.

- **`src/find_best_mobo/commands/estimate.py`** — `project`'s only call site. The plan puts the signature in slice 3 and asserts in slice 1 that the command already passes submissions. It does not, and cannot: slice 1 may not change `project`. So the call site is homeless, and leaving it would not compile. One line.
- **`tests/test_estimate_coverage.py`** — constructs `Projection` directly and calls `project` seven times. A dataclass gaining required fields breaks it. The fixture is held at a neutral all-excerpts corpus, since that file is about the coverage line and not about routing. No test deleted or weakened.

### Two more places the plan is short

- **The rendered cap has nowhere to live.** The plan requires the cap printed but names no field for it, and `render_projection(projection)` takes nothing else. A `bundle_token_cap` field carries it. The blind author hit the same gap and wrote its cap tests to assert the behaviour through `project()` rather than a field name, so they hold either way.
- **The Signatures block omits `coverage`**, which R1012 (OD-23) already put on `Projection` after this plan was written. It is kept, with its existing assertions untouched.

### Verified locally

1499 passing (45 new). `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean. `mypy src tests` clean over 45 files. `plan-resolve.sh` resolves this plan. `blind-tests.sh` reports `tests/test_estimate.py` unmodified since its authoring commit. `acceptance-criteria.sh` green.
